title: Train and audit a small reward model
outcome: Perform actual CPU gradient updates on a tiny reward predictor and expose a length shortcut using independent comparison features.

exercises.title: Verify the initial gradient
exercises.task: Compare autograd at zero weights with \(D^{\mathsf T}(0.5-y)/n\).
exercises.expected: The two vectors match in float64.
exercises.hint: Use pairwise feature differences as rows.
exercises.answer: The check tests the implemented likelihood and reduction denominator independently of whether the labels are meaningful.

exercises.title: Inspect the length coefficient
exercises.task: Train the balanced design in case A.
exercises.expected: The length coefficient remains approximately zero.
exercises.hint: Its two tie comparisons are symmetric.
exercises.answer: The authored design provides no systematic signal that longer is preferable, so the symmetric initialization and updates preserve the zero length direction.

exercises.title: Reverse a comparison
exercises.expected: The linear reward margin changes sign.
exercises.answer: This is a useful implementation invariant for a pairwise difference model.

exercises.title: Find a training shortcut
exercises.task: Inspect the weights from case B.
exercises.expected: Length receives more weight than either evidence coordinate.
exercises.hint: The biased design makes length strongly predictive of labels.
exercises.answer: An optimizer fits the provided associations. It cannot infer the intended target when the comparison design leaves that target confounded.

exercises.title: Recompute the final loss
exercises.task: Evaluate the objective after the final optimizer step.
exercises.expected: The final-state loss is distinct from the last pre-update loss.
exercises.hint: Logging order is part of the artifact identity.
exercises.answer: A reported result should identify the model state that produced it, especially when comparing training and held-out measurements.

exercises.title: State the model boundary
exercises.task: Describe what the three learned weights establish.
exercises.expected: A real small CPU reward fit, with no natural-language capability claim.
exercises.hint: Identify the representation and its provenance.
exercises.answer: The exercise uses authored features. It does not train a language encoder, judge real responses or establish the preferences of an external population.

sources: PyTorch binary cross entropy with logits
